note: Shape vectors for 'swarma release-manifest/0', round 4 (one manifest per release set). ALL vectors here are shape-only: every digest and commit is synthetic, no digest is the digest of a real file, and no vector carries an approved digest. 'expect' is the result of the verifier's SHAPE mode defined in 03-verifier-contract.md: checks V-04 to V-12 on the file bytes, then V-13 and V-14 under the host named by 'host' (default 'host_default'). The closed result set of shape mode is 'shape_ok' plus the refusal codes of V-04 to V-14. 'shape_ok' is a result of shape mode only; it is not a result of the advisory or the authoritative mode, and it never means approved. Every file except index.json, unpack-cases.json and invalid-07 is one line of canonical bytes with no trailing line feed. Round 4 change: invalid-26 now varies exactly one member of valid-01 ('format'); its artifact 'name' is again valid-01's.

not_shipped_as_files.reason: these depend on how the approved digest is supplied, not on a manifest file; rows with valid neighbours are in 03-verifier-contract.md
they need a file system object with a given owner, mode, type or link count, or a file larger than 65536 bytes that the implementer generates

it needs a computed SHA-256; the producer could compute none. Harness rule: take valid-01, compute its digest D, supply D (expect the run to pass V-03) and supply D with its last digit changed (expect this code).

variants not shipped: a byte-order mark, invalid UTF-8 and a non-ASCII byte need exact bytes the producer could not write or check; an escape sequence in a string, an exponent form (1e3) and container depth 6 are plain ASCII and are left to the implementer's generator, each with valid-01 as the neighbour. A negative integer in shortest form is canonical bytes and is NOT this code: it is invalid-34 (V-10).
bound variants not shipped as files: 33 products, 5 artifacts in one product, a 129-byte name, a 64-byte label, a value above 9007199254740991; each is generated from valid-01
depends on the host, not on the file; harness rule: run valid-01 with host 'darwin/arm64' (expect this code) and with 'linux/amd64' (expect shape_ok)

it needs two real files with computed digests, built from real bytes (never a preimage of a synthetic digest, and never by varying a byte-source artifact, which V-18 would refuse first). Harness rule: (1) write a package file P of arbitrary bytes and compute its SHA-256 d and its length; (2) write a canonical manifest M whose first-install product's selected artifact has 'sha256' d and 'size' equal to the length of P (the other products of M may be copied from valid-01 with their own real files, or M is valid-01 with only that artifact's 'sha256' and 'size' replaced by d and the length), compute the set digest of M and supply it as the approved digest; (3) place P in the byte source under the name d, so V-16 to V-18 pass; (4) run authoritative mode with P itself as the protected first-install package copy ('first-install/package'): expect the run to pass V-19; then run it again with P changed in exactly one byte as 'first-install/package' (the byte source still holds the original P under d, so V-18 still passes): expect 'first_install_mismatch' with the first-install product as the subject. Valid neighbour: the same run with the unmodified P as the package copy.

they need the second-build comparison record of the test profile (TP-6), whose byte encoding is MISSING (owner: the installer specification), and real artifact digests. Harness rule, in V-20's stated order: an authoritative run over a verified protected directory with no comparison record returns 'second_build_missing'; the same run with a record whose own digest differs from the approved comparison-record digest returns 'second_build_mismatch' before any byte of it is parsed; the same run with an approved record that omits one selected artifact, lists an artifact not in the set, carries a manifest digest for a selected artifact that differs from the manifest, or carries a second-build digest that differs from that manifest digest, returns 'second_build_mismatch' by computation (its equality flag, where the encoding has one, is audit-only: a record that marks an artifact equal while its two digests differ still returns 'second_build_mismatch', and a record whose two digests are equal passes this part even if its flag disagrees); the same run with a complete approved record whose manifest digest and second-build digest are equal for every selected artifact passes V-20. Advisory mode runs the same rule over the account's own copy with the digests typed by the person.

not_shipped_as_files.expect: set_too_large, storage_insufficient, artifact_unavailable, artifact_unprotected, artifact_size_mismatch, artifact_digest_mismatch, provenance_missing, provenance_invalid, io_error, record_write_failed, verified, advisory_ok
not_shipped_as_files.reason: they need real artifact files, computed digests or a protected directory; each has a row with a valid neighbour in 03-verifier-contract.md. The provenance codes belong to the product profile, which v0 does not define; on the test profile V-20 takes the second-build record instead (TP-6).
